findings.summary: The middle panel, the iron's share of the stray field, does not let a reader see its data. One +6787 % spike at R-R_edge = 0.294 m sets a linear axis spanning about -442 to 7131 %, so the -96 % share held from 0.5 m to 11.5 m on all three planes, which is the section's headline result, is drawn as a ~4 px band 2 px below zero and is further covered by the 2 px solid black zero line that scripts/iron_field_source/figure.py:88 draws after the curves. A reader sees a flat line at about 0 % where the plotted values are -96 %, so the panel shows the opposite sign. The ink confirms it: 655 of the panel's 797 teal pixels sit in rows 556-560, inside and just beneath the black rule at rows 555-556. The same -96 % figure survives only in the prose table beside the figure, not in the picture.

The three with-iron curves nearly coincide (0.255, 0.262 and 0.269 mT at 1 m), and because the loop draws midplane, Fb and then Fh, the teal overprints the other two: beyond x = 2 m the render carries 56 blue px and 56 orange px against 905 teal px. findings.summary: The same three-entry plane legend is drawn twice on one figure, in the upper panel (line 62) and again in the middle panel (line 92), with none in the lower panel. The colours mean the same three planes in both panels, so one figure-level legend would carry it; the repeated block spends vertical space in a figure that already has three stacked panels and narrows the plot area of each.
